full_judgment: 13. The last point argued by the learned Advocate for the petitioner was that in view of the fact that the trial court "presumed that the plaintiffs did not possess the land since auction purchase" on the ground of non-payment of rent by them, the appellate Court erred in law in allowing the appeal without altering the aforesaid finding of the trial court. There is no legal presumption against a person who fails to pay rent for a long time. Mere non-payment of rent cannot take away the right, title, interest and possession of the plaintiffs and the learned Munsif was wrong in presuming that the plaintiffs are not in possession as they are not paying, rent for a long time. Non-consideration of this minor aspect of the case does not make the decision of the appellate Court illegal occasioning a failure of justice. I do not find any substance in the argument of the learned Advocate for the petitioner.
